layout_dets.text: CRITICAL CREVICE TEMPERATURE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: nickel alloys in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Edward L. Hibner*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Techniques exist presently for ranking alloys for crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance by determining their critical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice temperature (CCT) in 6 to 10%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments. Laboratory studies were conducted on nickel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys to evaluate the effect of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test procedure on CCT results. A modified test pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cedure was developed that yields more reproducible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , results with less data scatter than is incurred with exist-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing techniques. The severity of the environment in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creased with increasing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content from 6 to 10%.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The CCT results correlated with the alloy Cr, Mo, Cb, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: W content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: USING IDENTICAL TEST PROCEDURES, both the Materials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Technology Institute (MTl) of the chemical process industry

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the Pulp and Paper Research Institute of Canada (PPRIC)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been involved in ranking alloys by critical crevice temper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ature (CCT) valves in 6 and 10% FeCl₃ environments, respec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively.1,2 Modifications were made to the MTI test procedures,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which yield the most reproducible CCTs for nickel alloys in 6%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FeCl3 (i.e., 10%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for 24-h exposure. The modified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MT! test procedure will provide an excellent way to rank can-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: didate alloys as to crevice corrosion resistance in severe ox-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: idizing chloride environments. An accurate estimate of an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy's CCT can be made based on its CR, Mo, Cb, and W con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tent.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The test material came from commercially produced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.062-in. (1.57-mm) and 0.125-in. (3.25-mm) sheet. Table 1 shows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the nominal chemical compositions of the evaluated alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Crevice corrosion specimens were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in. (51 × 51 mm) by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sheet thickness. The specimens were fitted with multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice devices produced by TFE-fluorocarbon washers of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: type described by Anderson.³ Before initial testing, all speci-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mens were given a 120-grit surface finish with aluminum oxide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paper and cleaned with acetone. The test solutions were pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pared by dissolving reagent-grade

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into distilled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: water. CCTs were determined by both the MTI procedure in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Manual No. 3 of May 1980 and a modification thereof.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the MTi procedure, duplicate specimens are exposed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for 24 h at a fixed temperature. If no attack of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any type is observed, the sample is considered to be immune

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at that temperature and is further exposed, without resanding,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for another 24 h at a 2.5 C higher temperature. This procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is continued until attack is observed. As mentioned, PPRiC

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uses an identical test procedure, but the CCT values are deter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mined in 10%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (not hexahydrate). The MTl procedure was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modified by resanding and cleaning the crevice corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specimens before further exposure of the specimen at highei

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperatures. Least squares fit was used to determine lines in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the CCT plots.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Results and discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In review, the CCT test is a method designed to determine

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the relative resistance of alloys to crevice corrosion in oxidiz-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing chloride environments by measuring the minimum (critical)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature for crevice corrosion initiation. The higher the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CCT, the greater the crevice resistance. At room temperature,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has a natural pH of 1.2 to 1.3.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Data scatter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table 2 contains CCT values for nickel alloys evaluated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 6% FeCl3 by both the MTI and the modified MTI procedure.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results are compared to PPRIC literature CCT values,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: determined in 10%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (not hexahydrate), for Alloys 825, G,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 625, and C-276. Generally, CCT values determined by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: original MTl procedure in 6%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: agree better with the litera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture CCT values determined in 10%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than those from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modified MTI procedure do.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Greater data scatter was observed by the MTI procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than by the modified MTi procedure. Using the MTi procedure,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6 of the 14 alloys (heats) displayed variances of 2.5 to 5.0 C in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duplicate specimens. With the modified MTI procedure, only 3

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 15 alloys (heats) displayed variances of only 2.5 C in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duplicate specimens.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figures 1 and 2 áre plots of the CCT vs alloy Mo content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as determined by the MTI and modified MTI procedures,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: respectively. Figure 3 compares the lines taken from Figures 1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 2. Lower CCT values were obtained with the modified pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cedure than by the originai MTI procedure. The difference was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: greater with higher alloy Mo content. Perhaps the higher CCT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: values associated with the original MTi and PPRIC procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the greater data scatter observed for the original MTl pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cedure relate to surface passivation. In the MTI procedure, the
